comments.author: @giannisolga5191
comments.text: I enjoyed this video immensely. Seeing Ernst Meyer, who is a legend, and seeing him in the context of PNG. Now I understand why the biologist Jared Diamond keeps coming back to PGN. Wonderful pictures of cassawaries. I thought they were carnivorous. The tree kangaroo blew me away, and the little joey was so cute. What better proof that evolution will fill empty niches. Anthropologists described the cargo plane cult, PNGers had never seen planes, thought they were gods and set up altars to them. Exploitation, extractive industries that threaten Mother Earth everywhere have discovered PNG too. Your comments that languages are world views, unique perceptions of reality, were very profound. The aerial view were truly spectacular. Very grateful for this video.

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: That connection to Ernst Mayr is a wonderful one to make - his time in PNG really did shape decades of evolutionary biology that followed, Jared Diamond included. Glad the cassowaries and especially that tree kangaroo joey landed the way they did; evolution filling empty niches is exactly the right lens for how strange and wonderful PNG's wildlife turned out. And the cargo cult detail is one of anthropology's most fascinating and often misunderstood chapters. Thank you for such a generous, thoughtful read of the whole thing.
